hook.en: Fill in the blanks with suitable prepositions; use the right form of the verb; correct the error. These short items carry marks that careful students never lose.

objectives.en: Use prepositions correctly after common verbs, nouns and adjectives

narration.en: Fill in the blanks with suitable prepositions; use the right form of the verb; correct the error. These short items carry marks that careful students never lose.

body.en: Many words take a fixed preposition: good at, afraid of, interested in, fond of, prefer to, insist on, accuse someone of, congratulate on, comply with, abide by, superior to, senior to, different from, divide into, according to. Time: at 6 o'clock, on Monday, in May, since 2015 (point of time), for two years (period). Place: at the station, in the room, on the table. Learn them in phrases, not as single words.

title.en: On the board: phrasal verbs with meanings

say.en: A phrasal verb is a verb with a particle; the meaning can change completely.

text.en: put off = postpone           put up with = tolerate
look into = investigate     look up to = respect
give up = stop trying       give in = surrender
call off = cancel           bring up = raise; mention
turn down = reject          carry out = perform
The match was called off because of rain.
I cannot put up with this noise any longer.
The police are looking into the complaint.

explanation.en: The particle changes the meaning: put off, put up with and put out mean quite different things.

body.en: Subject–verb agreement: the verb agrees with the real subject (One of the boys is absent; Each of the students has a book; The quality of the mangoes was poor). Either/neither … or/nor: the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Tenses: no future after if or when in a time clause (When he comes, I will tell him); the present perfect is not used with a past time (I saw him yesterday, not I have seen him yesterday). Uncountable nouns (information, advice, furniture, luggage) take no plural.

points.en: One of the + plural noun + singular verb
Neither … nor: verb agrees with the nearer subject
No present perfect with yesterday, ago, last …

passage.en: She has been living in Chennai __1__ 2018. He was accused __2__ cheating, but he insisted __3__ his innocence. Our team is far superior __4__ theirs.

explanation.en: since + point of time; accused of; insisted on; superior to (never "superior than").

problem.en: Correct the errors: (a) Each of the players have a new kit. (b) I have met him yesterday. (c) She gave me many advices.

steps.en: (a) The subject is "each", which is singular: Each of the players has a new kit.
(b) A finished past time (yesterday) needs the simple past: I met him yesterday.
(c) Advice is uncountable: She gave me a lot of advice (or many pieces of advice).

answer.en: (a) has (b) met (c) a lot of advice
